title: pEGASUS-HPC in the Management of Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis: A Retrospective Single- Center Experience
content: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) is a challenging cause of acute large vessel occlusion (LVO), and elective treatment when refractory to medical therapy remains controversial. The pEGASUS HPC is a novel, low-profile, hydrophilic-coated stent designed to reduce thrombogenicity. We retrospectively evaluated its safety and efficacy in both rescue and elective settings. Between December 2022 and December 2024, 40 consecutive patients were treated at our center. Twenty-seven underwent rescue stenting for ICAS-related LVO after ≥3 failed thrombectomy passes or early re-occlusion. Thirteen received elective stenting for symptomatic ICAS meeting WEAVE on-label criteria. Technical success, 24-hour and long-term patency, hemorrhagic complications, and 90-day outcomes (mRS) were assessed. Technical success (final TICI 2b–3) was achieved in 93% of rescue and 100% of elective cases. In the rescue group, symptomatic and asymptomatic hemorrhage occurred in 19% and 22% of patients, with 96% 24-hour and 95% long-term patency; 86% achieved mRS &lt;2 at 90 days. In the elective group, 8% experienced both symptomatic and asymptomatic hemorrhage, with 100% 24-hour and 90% long-term patency; 90% achieved mRS &lt;2. These findings suggest that pEGASUS HPC stenting is feasible and safe in both settings. Prospective trials are needed to confirm its role and refine antiplatelet regimens.
